about: Every change made to the digital Gita Press text, and every reading in which the independent witnesses differ and the Gita Press reading was kept. check.py fails if a logged correction does not match text.json.

corrections.reason: सिंहृति is not a word. The sense (“in the form of dissolution at the end”) needs संहृति, and both witnesses (GRETIL MkP 81.57, Freund) read संहृतिरूपान्ते.
The line is a list of feminine nominatives (महाविद्या महामाया महामेधा …); महास्मृतः is masculine and leaves the second pāda one syllable short. Both witnesses read महास्मृतिः.
Footnote marker of the printed book carried into the text; the footnote is Hindi commentary, not part of the mantra.
Footnote marker of the printed book carried into the text.

A space inside one word: महासिंहम् ‘the great lion’ (object of उत्थाय, ‘mounting’), as both witnesses (GRETIL MkP 87, Freund) print it. Split as महासिम् + हम् the line yields an unattested ‘great sword’ with a stray syllable.

corrections.from: a fourth block numbered 30 repeating एवं देव्या वरं लब्ध्वा सुरथः क्षत्रियर्षभः। सूर्याज्जन्म समासाद्य सावर्णिर्भविता मनुः॥ क्लीं ॐ॥
corrections.to: 13.28 and 13.29 as printed; the closing क्लीं ॐ moved to 13.29
corrections.reason: The digital file repeats the last one and a half lines as a block numbered 30. The chapter's own colophon counts 29 mantras (uvāca 6, half-ślokas 11, ślokas 12; 700 in all), which the repetition would break.

corrections.from: zero-width joiners (U+200D), non-breaking and doubled spaces
corrections.reason: Rendering hints for half-forms (सद्‍वृत्ता) carry no letter; removing them lets every word be compared and transliterated exactly.

corrections.from: bīja syllables printed around the first and last mantra of each chapter (‘ॐ’ ऐं, ॐ ह्रीं, ॐ क्लीं … ऐं ॐ, ॐ, ह्रीं ॐ (4.42), क्लीं ॐ)
corrections.reason: They belong to the recitation (the sampuṭa of the Gita Press pāṭha), not to the Mārkaṇḍeya text. They are shown with the mantra but are not analysed as words of the verse.

variants.note: Kept as the Gita Press reading; check against the printed book.
Same form; doubling of the stop before its aspirate is a common printing convention.
The Gita Press spells the n + ś sandhi out (ñch); the witnesses leave it unapplied.
The same word (nairṛtī, the power of Nirṛti); र्ऋ is a printing convention.
In the kept reading सा देवी is the subject of यत्रास्ते (“where that Devī stayed”), and the messenger is the speaker.

variants.other: a third line, अश्वांश्च पातयामास रथं सारथिना सह
variants.note: Not in the Gita Press text; its colophon (27 ślokas, 1 half-śloka) agrees with the two-line form.
The kept form is the one generally recited.
The Gita Press marks the avagraha: mahā + avidyā, “great nescience”, balancing महारात्रि. Without it the word is mahāvidyā, “great knowledge”. Both readings are traditional.

recension_notes: GRETIL's Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa (adhyāyas 81–93) carries several verses the Gita Press text does not (e.g. after 1.101, in 2.20, 2.45, 2.65, 3.21, 3.43). They belong to the Purāṇa recension; the Gita Press 700 is the recited Saptaśatī and is followed here. Nothing was added to it.

GRETIL counts ślokas in pairs of half-lines and does not number the uvāca lines, so its verse numbers differ from the Gita Press mantra numbers throughout. This edition numbers by the Gita Press mantra.

metre_notes.note: The third pāda (the first of the second printed line), मधुकैटभौ दुरात्मानौ, is nine syllables (hypermetric), as in every witness.
The third pāda (the first of the second printed line), महिषेऽसुराणामधिपे, is nine syllables, as in every witness.
